newsitem.title: USA: Novellus drops as Q1 book-to-bill falls short.
newsitem.headline: Novellus drops as Q1 book-to-bill falls short.

text.p: Shares of Novellus Systems Inc dropped sharply Monday after the chip equipment maker said its first quarter book-to-bill ratio fell short of one-to-one and that the company may face potential financial damage from a patent infringement lawsuit.
Novellus sank 18-1/4 to 57-1/4 in heavy trading.
The book-to-bill ratio is a key indicator of sales trends. A ratio of one-to-one means that for every $100 of equipment shipped, $100 of new orders were booked.
Novellus also said its first quarter earnings dropped to $0.91 a share from $1.55 a share last year.
San Jose, Calif.-based Novellus also said its first quarter net sales dropped 12 percent to $101.7 million from $115.3 million last year.

"Despite the decrease in net sales and net income from the prior year, we feel that our business has held up well given the severity of the industry downturn. We are pleased that we are able to continue to generate record quarterly levels in cash and short-term investments," said Robert Smith, Novellus' chief financial officer.
Cash and short-term investments as of March 29 were $183.5 million, a record quarterly amount and up four percent from $176.7 million at the end of 1996, Novellus said.
Separately, Novellus said it will seek to overturn a patent infringement jury verdict against it in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California.
The jury verdict found that Novellus had infringed on a semiconductor processing patent held by Applied Materials Inc.
Novellus warned that potential damages from the case could have a material adverse impact on the company.

"To the extent that our defenses are not upheld, the amount of damages which could be assessed against the company would have a material adverse impact on our results of operations in the fiscal period recorded and could have a material adverse impact on the company's financial condition," the company said in a prepared statement.
"In addition, depending on the scope of any injunction entered by the court, the company's future operating results could be materially and adversely affected," the company said.
